INSTANCE: the value of `predicate` of a VSA Statement (predicateType https://slsa.dev/verification_summary/v1). Required and optional are the words of section 3.2 (L123-222): verifier, resourceUri, policy, verificationResult, verifiedLevels required; timeVerified, inputAttestations, dependencyLevels, slsaVersion, verifier.version optional. Sub-requirements: policy MUST contain uri (SHOULD contain digest) (L171-172); an inputAttestations entry MUST contain digest (SHOULD contain uri) (L184-185); verificationResult is either PASSED or FAILED (L190). Unrecognized fields are NOT constrained: consumers MUST ignore them (L110) and producers MAY add URI-named extension fields (L115), so no additionalProperties keyword is set (tests ACCEPT-ignored-field and ACCEPT-uri-extension pin this). dependencyLevels admits null: L213-214 distinguish an unset or null dependencyLevels from an empty object although L205 types it as object (marked inferred). Counts are integers >= 0: the schema block says <Int> (L98) and the text calls them a count of dependencies (L207); the minimum 0 is inferred. READINGS WHERE THE SOURCE IS SILENT (not bound, see schema-tests silent cases): timeVerified, verifier.id and resourceUri are strings with no format check (their types [Timestamp], [TypeURI], [ResourceURI] are defined in in-toto, outside this source); digest is an object with no value constraint ([DigestSet] outside this source); policy and inputAttestations entries are [ResourceDescriptor]s, whose other fields (name, downloadLocation, mediaType, content, annotations) are outside this source and tolerated; verifiedLevels may be empty and may contain FAILED beside other values; the relation of verificationResult to a FAILED element is not stated; digest SHOULD-presence on policy and uri SHOULD-presence on entries are not enforced (SHOULD). NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN JSON SCHEMA: one level per SLSA track in verifiedLevels (L199) is semantic rule SEM-01 in check-schemas.derived.py; that inputAttestations contains ALL attestations used (L181-182) and each dependency is counted once, at its highest level (L216-219), cannot be checked from the document.
